topic.angle: How many people miss a gorilla while counting passes

body.question: Viewers counted basketball passes in a video. What percentage failed to notice a person in a gorilla suit walking through?
body.reveal: About half of viewers missed the gorilla. Focusing hard on one task can hide even something obvious. This is called inattentional blindness.

probes.question: About what percentage of viewers missed the gorilla in the famous attention experiment?

image_brief.show: A basketball game or a person in a gorilla costume (illustration is fine); no recognisable real person

claims.claim: Viewers counted basketball passes in a video
claims.quote: count the passes made by one of the teams

claims.claim: A person in a gorilla suit walks through
About half (50%) failed to notice the gorilla
claims.quote: In most groups, 50% of the subjects did not report seeing the gorilla.
claims.note: 'Most groups' - figure varies by group; 'about half' fair.

claims.claim: Focusing on one task can hide something obvious; called inattentional blindness
claims.quote: fails to perceive an unexpected stimulus in plain sight because their attention is focused elsewhere.
In most groups, 50% of the subjects did not report seeing the gorilla.
